**Setup.** The slots are S1a (screen 1, 7 P.M.), S1b (screen 1, 9 P.M.), S2a (screen 2, 7 P.M.), S2b (screen 2, 9 P.M.) and S3 (screen 3, 8 P.M.). The start times are therefore 7, 7, 8, 9, 9.

**Fixing three movies.** The romance begins before the western, and the western begins before the horror film. So romance < western < horror in start time, with all three times distinct. The only way to get three distinct increasing times is 7, 8, 9, so:
- Romance is at 7 P.M.
- Western is at 8 P.M., which is screen 3.
- Horror is at 9 P.M.

The romance is not on screen 2, so it is in S1a. The horror film is at 9 P.M. on either screen 1 or screen 2. The mystery and sci-fi take the two remaining slots.

**Case 1: horror in S1b.** The remaining slots are S2a and S2b, both on screen 2. The mystery and sci-fi fill them, and the mystery is on a different screen from the horror film, as required. Sci-fi is on screen 2.

**Case 2: horror in S2b.** The remaining slots are S1b and S2a. The mystery cannot share screen 2 with the horror film, so the mystery is in S1b and sci-fi is in S2a. Sci-fi is on screen 2.

**Checking the options.**
- A fails in Case 2, where horror is on screen 2.
- B fails in both cases. In Case 1 the mystery can be at 9 P.M. (S2b), and in Case 2 it is at 9 P.M. (S1b).
- C fails in Case 2, where the mystery is on screen 1.
- D fails in Case 2, where sci-fi is at 7 P.M.
- E holds in both cases.
